top_5_failure_modes.name: Severe Escalation False Negatives (Frustration, Prior Failed Contacts, Carrier Impasse)
top_5_failure_modes.description: Customer experiences severe friction (e.g. 2-3 previous failed contacts, carrier lost package, no resolution), yet the model predicts escalate=False and provides standard self-service steps.
top_5_failure_modes.root_cause_hypothesis: The prompt's escalation guidelines prioritize safety and self-service default without a dedicated sentiment/re-contact detection classifier or calibrated threshold.
top_5_failure_modes.mitigation: Add explicit few-shot rules for prior-contact signals ('2nd/3rd time contacting', 'nobody knows', 'unresolved') and implement a dedicated multi-stage escalation classifier with higher sensitivity.

top_5_failure_modes.name: ORDER_STATUS Underprediction & Confusion with DELIVERY_DELAY / REFUND_PENDING
top_5_failure_modes.description: Customers inquiring about overall order state or shipments before dispatch are misclassified into downstream execution states like DELIVERY_DELAY or REFUND_PENDING.
top_5_failure_modes.root_cause_hypothesis: Keywords like 'dispatch', 'prepared for shipment', or 'cancel' trigger specific operational branch prompts rather than general status lookups.
top_5_failure_modes.mitigation: Clarify taxonomy definition: pre-shipment timeline inquiries belong to ORDER_STATUS, whereas confirmed past-due shipments belong to DELIVERY_DELAY.

top_5_failure_modes.name: DELIVERY_DELAY vs PACKAGE_NOT_RECEIVED Ambiguity
top_5_failure_modes.description: In-transit carrier delays (courier not answering, redelivery attempt) get classified as lost packages (PACKAGE_NOT_RECEIVED).
top_5_failure_modes.root_cause_hypothesis: Semantic overlap between 'item has not arrived yet' (delay) and 'package is permanently lost/missing' (not received).
top_5_failure_modes.mitigation: Refine prompt boundary: use PACKAGE_NOT_RECEIVED only when carrier marks delivered or explicitly lost; use DELIVERY_DELAY when tracking indicates active transit/redelivery.

top_5_failure_modes.name: PRODUCT_ISSUE Confusion with CUSTOMER_SERVICE_CONTACT / ACCOUNT_SUPPORT
top_5_failure_modes.description: Customers describing software/hardware defects (app crashing, review submission failure, server errors) are classified as general contact or account issues.
top_5_failure_modes.root_cause_hypothesis: When customers ask 'can someone help with this error in the app', the contact intent overrides the technical defect intent.
top_5_failure_modes.mitigation: Prioritize domain-specific technical defects over generic contact intent when an explicit app/device malfunction is described.

top_5_failure_modes.name: REFUND_PENDING Overprediction on Return / Order Status Queries (Low Precision = 31.25%)
top_5_failure_modes.description: Any customer message mentioning return, cancellation, or money is prematurely classified as REFUND_PENDING even before a return or refund has been initiated.
top_5_failure_modes.root_cause_hypothesis: High semantic salience of refund keywords in the embedding/prompt matching logic.
top_5_failure_modes.mitigation: Restrict REFUND_PENDING to cases where a refund has already been authorized or return received, routing pre-return questions to PRODUCT_ISSUE or ORDER_STATUS.

escalation_failure_breakdown.conclusion: The system missed 42 of 46 escalation-positive examples (91.3%). Repeated unresolved prior support contact was the largest missed subgroup (19/42), but the failures also included carrier deadlocks, severe frustration, financial/account stalemates, and persistent technical issues.

limitation_notes.inter_model_agreement: Because the secondary quality audit was performed by an independent LLM rather than a human evaluator, inter-model agreement should not be interpreted as human validation.
